# Interface catalog

It writes no record of its own; the deal and the owner's pick are written in the change's design section. The design step owns the ask, the showing and the lock, and the interface rules own every constraint a measurement can check.

## How the deal is drawn

The deal draws three directions, each a material, a palette, a type pairing, a composition and a motion register, from the entries that serve the register and the platform in play: a site's heroes and page shapes, an app's shells and screen patterns. The page's job gives the anatomy, the same for the three. The tone, the sector and the material in hand weight the draw toward the entries whose words name them, and a composition that needs pictures is never dealt to a product that has none. The three differ entry by entry. The same ask deals the same three, and the owner may reroll once.

passages.text:
## Reading an entry

An entry is data. Its tokens stand in DESIGN.md's groups, so a pick writes into the design system with no translation; its sketch is rows, columns and the slot each region holds; its words give its reasons and its pitfalls. Its colours come with the ink-on-ground pairs they are read in, each meeting the floor. A constraint a measurement can check belongs to the interface rules, never to an entry. An entry names where its language came from, a source at its commit or a site studied on the day it was seen, and the source's own expression stays out of it.

# Interface catalog: the practice's mechanics

This page holds where the catalog's data stands and its commands. Read it with `SKILL.md` when the work lands in the workspace.

passages.text:
## Where it stands

- The entries are `catalog/entries.json` in this skill's folder, one schema for every entry: its id, kind, register, platform, facets, tokens, contrast pairs, sketch, words and provenance. Never paste the file whole into a reply or a record; deal from it.
- A pick names its entries by their ids in the record's design section, beside the owner's words.
passages.reason: Where the entries stand beside the skill and how a pick names them (J-123 S6).
passages.gist: Where the entries stand and how a pick names them

passages.text:
## Commands

- `greenline deal --register <site or app> --job <the page's job> --tone <words> --material <what is in hand>` deals three directions and prints the seed it drew under; the same ask deals the same three, `--reroll` draws once again on the owner's word alone, and the harness hook refuses a `--seed` the owner's words did not name and a `--reroll` they did not ask for, or a second one, and `--json` prints the entries' ids alone.
- `greenline inspect` shows the three side by side in its deal view, whose pick button writes `.greenline/ledger/<id>/design-pick.json`, and the catalog's entries as specimens in the Atlas's catalog.
passages.reason: The deal's command and the viewer's deal view and catalog browser (J-123 S6). J-149 S4: the deal's three come from the ask, a seed scan and an unasked reroll refused by the hook with the owner's words as the exit.
